narrative:
On October 7, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 40.8%, taking up 1,240 of the 3,036 scheduled matters across 51 judges. This marks a modest rise from the 39.6% hearing rate recorded on October 6 (1,224 heard of 3,090), though performance remains slightly below the 41.7% achieved on October 5 and the 46.4% seen on October 1.

Judge-level throughput showed significant variation across heavy rosters. Justice K.S. Hemalekha led in total cases heard, completing 67 of 124 scheduled matters (54.0%), closely followed by Justice G. Basavaraja with 65 of 110 cases heard (59.1%) and Justice C.M. Poonacha with 60 of 102 matters (58.8%). In contrast, Court Hall 1 recorded zero hearings across 39 listed cases, Justice K.V. Aravind took up 30 of 153 scheduled cases (19.6%), and Justice Hanchate Sanjeevkumar heard 27 of 128 matters (21.1%).

Across procedural stages, preliminary hearings logged the strongest progress among major stages at 49.5% (216 of 436). Orders and admission lists maintained steady throughput at 41.7% (402 of 963) and 41.6% (316 of 759) respectively, matching recent benchmarks. Final hearings showed a notable recovery, converting 31.5% of scheduled cases (178 of 565), up from 19.3% on October 6 and 22.7% on October 5.

In terms of case distribution, Writ Petitions comprised the largest category, converting 41.0% (559 of 1,363), a minor dip from 42.1% on October 6 and 48.0% on October 5. Criminal Petitions reached a 44.1% hearing rate (212 of 481), while Criminal Appeals saw robust clearance at 57.6% (117 of 203). Civil appellate matters lagged behind, with Miscellaneous First Appeals posting a 35.1% hearing rate (149 of 424) and Regular First Appeals converting just 23.7% (28 of 118).
